newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus opposition defiant after arrests.
newsitem.headline: Belarus opposition defiant after arrests.

text.p: Belarus opposition forces were preparing for fresh protests on Saturday against President Alexander Lukashenko, refusing to back down after police beat and arrested dozens of demonstrators in Minsk on Friday.

"We have seen that the authorities dealt with protesters in a very brutal manner. They want to frighten us," said Leonid Vasyuchenko, who was on duty at the headquarters of the opposition Popular Front on Friday night.
"I think that on Saturday the authorities will be more violent. But we're not afraid. We will demand guarantees for our rights and freedom," Vasyuchenko told Reuters.

Police beat protesters and arrested about 50 people during an unsanctioned rally in the centre of the capital. Several journalists and two opposition politicians were among those bundled into two trucks and several police vehicles.
Some of those arrested looked dazed but there was no sign of bloodshed as police moved in to break up a gathering of up to 2,000 mostly young people.
Minsk authorities have also banned protesters from marching through the capital on Saturday, when opposition forces plan a large rally to mark Constitution Day.

The republic's first constitution was rewritten by the president last November. Despite vocal opposition that prompted anxious Russian mediation, Lukashenko won a landslide victory on expanding his powers in a controversial referendum.

The authorities have given permission for people to gather at noon (1000 GMT) on Saturday. But the opposition plans to assemble an hour earlier at a different square and to march about two km (a mile and a half) through central Minsk.

On Friday protesters were voicing their opposition to Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with neighbouring Russia, set in stone in a deal last year on forming a "commonwealth" of the two Slav states.
Kremlin leader Boris Yeltsin suggested on Friday that two countries might merge into a single state. The Belarussian leadership insists they remain two independent countries.
Police used truncheons and forced protesters to the ground after instructing them several times to clear the area.

Prominent opposition leaders Anatoly Lebedko and Boris Gunter were arrested as well as Pavel Severinets, the leader of the Popular Front's youth wing. Police earlier arrested Professor Yuri Khodyko, 53, the Front leader.
Authorities had sanctioned the Friday gathering but specifically banned protestors from proceeding through the city.

Lukashenko, facing growing unrest among opposition forces, has ordered restrictions on political meetings and banned his opponents from using post-independence national symbols, which he has scrapped in favour of old Soviet ones.
The press secretary for his policy-making Security Council, Vasily Baranov, accused the opposition of looking for a fight and of getting "more and more out of control".
State-run television said on Friday that the Minsk police behaved in "a correct manner according to European standards".
Some 60 deputies who refused to join the parliament set up under the new constitution met to call on the outside world not to recognise Lukashenko's new constitution.
The European Parliament still recognises the old parliament, saying the new one was formed illegally.

But Lukashenko praised his new constitution as a "guarantor of domestic political stability" in an address in official newspapers. "The updated constitution created a foundation for fulfilling the individual's rights and freedom," it said.
